claims.summary: Over any field, for P=sum_j q_j(x)(x_j^2-x_j), the class of q_j modulo all other Boolean equations is uniquely determined by P and represented by two successive divided differences in x_j at 0 and 1. A size-S depth-d division-free unbounded-fanin arithmetic circuit for P gives all v representatives in size O(v(S+1)^4), depth at most 4d+4, using the same field. These are representatives on coordinate lines, not a full correction tuple or multilinear normal forms in the remaining variables.
claims.assessment: Working monic-division and product-telescoping circuit argument, passed by the sole medium reviewer. No lower bound or generic canonicalization theorem.
claims.rationale: Tests whether full-coset coordinate-line data are hard: the invariant has a cheap representative computed from the already small residual.
claims.next_action: Check whether richer partial-coordinate data retain certificate information beyond these cheap line representatives, with full circuit and field costs.

claims.summary: For binary m-by-n A and n-by-m B, m>n>=1 and r=m-n, the formal residual P=product_(i,j)(1+delta_ij+(AB)_ij) vanishes after all but at most r individual entry variables are fixed to Boolean constants. A restriction leaving r+1 entries B_(n,j), j=n..m, free gives product_j t_j(1+t_j)^r, nonzero. Equivalently P lies in the ideal generated by products of r+1 distinct entry Boolean axioms, but not the analogous r+2 ideal; the witness also gives exact ordinary Boolean ideal order r+1. Every coefficient in every P=sum_j q_j(x)(x_j^2+x_j) is zero modulo all other Boolean equations. No circuit-size or PC-degree bound follows.
claims.assessment: Working sharp partial-coordinate and squarefree-support refinement of the recorded rank-residual order; passed by the sole medium reviewer. The coefficient conclusion is for the matching coordinate free and all other coordinates Boolean, not arbitrary parametrized lines.
claims.rationale: Strengthens the rank residual's ordinary multiplicity control to a sharp coordinate-cylinder statement and rules out one-coordinate information from every Boolean correction tuple.
claims.next_action: Assess full formal correction complexity beyond cheap partial-coordinate invariants; compare the squarefree Boolean support filtration with known small-product controls.

claims.summary: In the binary m-by-n rank-residual setting, r=m-n>=1, every restriction fixing all but exactly r+1 individual entry variables to Boolean constants gives either zero residual or P_T=(product_(e in T)(t_e^2+t_e))*H_T. Since the residual is a product of degree-at-most-two factors, cancelling the distinct linear factors t_e and t_e+1 leaves a product of factors of degree at most two, size O(m^2 n) and constant depth. For any chosen e in T, P_T=(t_e^2+t_e)Q_e has such a small quotient, hence a one-coefficient formal Boolean correction. No global assembly at this cost is established.
claims.assessment: Working factor-cancellation consequence of the sharp coordinate-freedom theorem, proposed by the existing reviewer, verified by the author and passed by the same reviewer's follow-up. No global assembly at this cost is established.
claims.rationale: Shows that even all minimally nonzero coordinate faces individually have cheap full corrections; this calibrates the proposed geometric extraction without claiming global circuit hardness.
claims.next_action: Test the cost of coherently combining face corrections, rather than treating separate local certificates or high support order as a lower bound.
